title: Fix weak WiFi signal on BCM43602 (MacBook Pro 2015-2017)
author: andyholst
body:
## Problem

MacBook Pro 2015-2017 with BCM43602 (brcmfmac) gets **-90 dBm** signal — barely usable past 1 meter.

The root cause is the NVRAM config loaded by the brcmfmac driver is too generic. It lacks proper power amplifier settings and antenna gain parameters for the MacBook's hinge-antenna design.

## What Didn't Fix It

1. options brcmfmac feature_disable=0x82000 — fixes WPA handshake, NOT signal
2. options cfg80211 ieee80211_regdom=US — fixes regulatory domain, NOT signal
3. roamoff=1 — reduces scanning retries, NOT signal
4. NVRAM config from Andy Holst (Bugzilla #193121) — helps channels, NOT signal

All help with **connecting** but NOT **signal strength**.

## Fix

Install cristianmiranda's improved NVRAM config which has proper board flags, antenna gain, and power amplifier parameters specific to MacBookPro13,3:

- boardflags=0x02000001 — proper board configuration (BT coexistence, PALDO)
- boardflags2=0xC0000000 — LNA bypass for 2G/5G clip, spur WAR
- boardflags3=0x40000108 — RCAL WAR, FEM table from NVRAM
- pa2ga0, pa2ga1 — 2.4GHz power amplifier settings
- pa5ga0, pa5ga1 — 5GHz power amplifier settings (all chains)
- maxp2ga0=74 — max power limits
- agbg0=2, aga0=2 — antenna gain
- Correct MAC address substitution from the running interface

The NVRAM config file is bundled directly in the repo — no download needed at install time.

## Result

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Signal | -90 dBm | -58 dBm |
| 5GHz | Unusable | 360 MBit/s |

32 dBm improvement — 5GHz now works reliably at full speed.

## Changes

| File | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| install/hardware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt | The NVRAM config bundled in repo |
| install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh | Detects BCM43602, installs config, rebuilds initramfs |
| install/hardware/all.sh | Runs the new fix during hardware setup |
| migrations/1786391101.sh | Applies fix to existing Omarchy installs |
| test/shell.d/brcmfmac-nvram-test.sh | 18 tests, all passing |

## Testing

```
ok - the NVRAM fix script exists
ok - script detects BCM43602 by PCI ID
ok - script installs the correct NVRAM file
ok - script handles MAC address substitution
ok - script rebuilds initramfs
ok - the NVRAM fix runs during hardware setup
ok - the NVRAM config source file exists
ok - NVRAM config contains MAC address placeholder
ok - NVRAM config contains boardflags
ok - NVRAM config contains 2GHz PA parameters
ok - NVRAM config contains 5GHz PA parameters
ok - NVRAM config was installed
ok - MAC address was substituted into NVRAM config
ok - boardflags parameter present
ok - 2GHz PA parameters present
ok - 5GHz PA parameters present
ok - boardflags2 parameter present
ok - boardflags3 parameter present
all tests passed
```
